MEL.definition: the list of items an aircraft may fly with unserviceable, and under what conditions

Deferral.definition: recording a defect as acceptable to fly with for a limited time, under the MEL
Deferral.inline: fly with the defect for a limited time

AOG.definition: aircraft on ground: not flyable until fixed

Tow-bar / pushback.definition: the bar connecting the tug to the nose wheel when the aircraft is pushed back from the stand
Tow-bar / pushback.inline: tug bar used to push the aircraft back

Stand / gate.definition: the parking position; a gate has a bridge or door to the terminal

Rotation.definition: the sequence of flights one aircraft is scheduled to fly today

Sector.definition: one flight from departure to arrival

Reactionary / knock-on delay.definition: delay to later flights caused by this one
Reactionary / knock-on delay.inline: delay passed on to later flights

FDP / duty margin.definition: the legal working hours remaining for the crew

Commander's discretion.definition: the captain's limited power to extend crew hours in specific circumstances
Commander's discretion.inline: captain's power to extend crew hours

MCC.definition: maintenance control, the engineers who decide technical questions

Certifying staff.definition: licensed engineers who may release an aircraft to fly
Certifying staff.inline: licensed engineers who sign the aircraft off

Occurrence report (MOR).definition: the mandatory safety report filed after an incident

EU261 / UK261.definition: the passenger-compensation rules for delays and cancellations

Ground handler.definition: the contractor providing stairs, buses, loading and pushback
